text:
caroline: Heads-up — enterprise lead (FinPlatform) asked for an estimate on Dedicated capacity for Q1 launch. They expect sustained 600 rps peak, 3 models concurrently (chat-medium, reranker, embeddings), and 99th perc latency target ~300ms.

aj: thanks. is 600 rps user-facing qps or internal request rate after batching?

caroline: they said 'requests' at the API level. We'll need to assume some batching and KV cache hit rate. Sales shared their traffic sample (attached).

ryan-sales: attaching summary from call: 600 rps peak, avg payload 512 tokens, 95% inference on chat-medium, 4% reranker, 1% embeddings. SLA required, no model quantization allowed.

jen-sre: no quantization means larger memory per model instance. Also sequence length variance matters — they have long tails to ~1k tokens. That affects KV cache and GPU memory.

dena: quick calc sketch: assume chat-medium avg generation = 150 output tokens, 512 input tokens, effective seq=662. With no quant, per-request GPU time ~? we should bench.

aj: I can run microbench on our Dedicated stage using chat-medium at seq=700 and batch sizes 8/16. will post numbers tonight.

capacity-bot: NOTE: existing Dedicated pool (prod-ded-1) has 40xA100-80GB reserved; baseline throughput for chat-medium @seq700 is ~45 rps per GPU at batch=8 (observed).

caroline: if that baseline holds, 600 rps / 45 rps ≈ 13.4 GPUs -> round up for redundancy and headroom. With autoscale + burst we'd want 20 GPUs reserved for predictability.

ryan-sales: customer prefers reserved capacity with burst to cloud. Their procurement wants a firm number for pricing — do we give 20 or 25?

jen-sre: give them 20 guaranteed + 10 burst. Pricing uses reserved commit for 20, burst at on-demand rates. We need to validate memory constraints: 3 models concurrently on the same GPU may not fit if models are large.

dena: question — are the reranker and embeddings run on the same GPU type? We can route embeddings to CPU or smaller GPU if latency tolerates it. That could reduce reserved GPU footprint.

aj: bench results (night): chat-medium @seq700: batch=8 -> 48 rps/GPU, p99=270ms; batch=16 -> 62 rps/GPU but p99 jumps to 520ms. So to hit 300ms p99 we must keep batch≤8 or use faster kernels.

caroline: perfect — use batch=8 baseline. Update calc: 600/48 = 12.5 -> 13 GPUs. Add 50% safety + 2 for redundancy => 21. I'll propose 20 reserved, 8 burst.

ryan-sales: sounds good. I'll draft the pricing note: reserved 20 GPUs (monthly commit), burst up to 28 GPUs with 15-min preemptible scale, SLA includes failover to alternate region on capacity loss.

jen-sre: add a rollout criteria item: we won't turn on heavy reranker traffic until we've validated multi-model co-residency on at least one customer environment. Add test plan: synthetic load with 3-model mix, KV cache hit patterns, and long-tail token bursts.

dena: I'll own bench for reranker+embeddings collocated. Also will test prefix caching and KV warmup impact. ETA 3 days.

caroline: next steps: (1) aj confirm numbers in prod-ded-1 and prod-like infra (done), (2) dena run collocation tests, (3) product -> produce an intake PR with proposed commit (20 GPUs), burst rules, and launch criteria.

ryan-sales: I'll tell the customer the proposed capacity and the constraints: we recommend no quantization but we may suggest a quantized variant if cost becomes blocking.

caroline: minor note for legal: contract needs explicit burst clauses and fallback policy. I'll loop in legal.

capacity-bot: ACTION_CREATED: intake-ticket #INT-5427 with assignees caroline, dena, aj.

caroline: Thanks everyone. I'll drop the intake PR and link here when ready. :thumbsup:

ryan-sales: TY!
